strips.evidence: About 2.4 m strip between the outer curb and the solid parking-edge line; cars stand in it at y 820-1000 (x 380-413). Empty near the crosswalk. C1 shows vehicles parked along the far curb of the opposing carriageway.

About 1.5 m strip between two parallel solid lines, lying between the parking strip and the single outbound travel lane. C1 shows two lines bounding a narrow strip next to the parked vehicles on the opposing carriageway. No bike symbol was visible on the satellite.

Single outbound travel lane (about 3.5 m) between the bicycle line and the planted median. It leaves the junction downstream of the crosswalk. In C1 and C2 the opposing traffic is on the far side of the median.

Raised median with grass and a row of trees, about 2.7 m wide, seen in C1 and C2 directly left of the inbound left-turn lane. On the satellite its two edges appear as faint curb lines, and its interior is darker (grass, warm colour in sunlit part at bottom). It ends before the crosswalk, where the crosswalk stripes run across it.

Left-turn lane between the median curb and the lane line at 626. It has a left-turn arrow on the satellite (x 580-610, y ~490-520), and C1 and C2 show a left-turn arrow and ONLY. The stop bar begins at the median curb (x ~560). It is still a full lane at S7 (C2, 55 m).
Through lane between lines 626 and 687, with a straight-ahead arrow on the satellite (x ~655) and in C1. The stop bar crosses it, partly hidden by a waiting car at x 630-665.

Narrow strip (about 1.3-1.5 m) between the solid bicycle line and the right curb. C1 shows a bicycle symbol and an arrow in it, and C2 shows the same narrow strip along the brick-edged curb. The stop bar extends faintly across it to x ~707. No right-turn marking or motor traffic seen in it.

trace.notes: S1 lies inside the junction, so every boundary is null there. S2 lies on the crosswalk (y ~281-342, slightly skewed), so only the outer curbs are given there. The stop bar is painted at y ~390 from the median curb to about x 707, with a car hiding x 630-665. Most of the road is in a building shadow, so the lightened panel was used. The median edges and both outer curbs are faint in the shadow and were placed from weak edge profiles, from sunlit patches (bottom of the crop, right corner) and from lane-width ratios in C1 and C2. Expect +/-5 units on those boundaries. The left (outbound) curb is mainly inferred from the parked cars and the crosswalk end (x ~384). The inbound bicycle line is faint between the stop bar and y ~520, but C1 shows it continuous, so S3 is interpolated. The outbound lines drift slightly toward the left approaching the crosswalk. Camera markers are a few metres off: C1 is drawn at x ~617, but the photo shows the camera in the through lane.

strips.evidence: Strip between the left kerb and a solid white edge line on the outbound (left) side. Parked cars stand in it on the satellite (x~310-348, y~560-850). C1 look-back shows a parked van and car outside a solid white line on the outbound kerb side, and C2 shows parked cars and parking T-marks between the kerb and that line. The strip narrows upstream, and in C2 the line closes on the kerb near the camera, so it is taken as ending by S7.

Single outbound travel lane between the parking edge line and the double yellow centre line (C1 and C2 both show one lane left of the double yellow). It starts at the downstream edge of the crosswalk (y~380).

Left-turn lane next to the centre line. The satellite shows left-turn arrows at y~525 and y~735, and C2 shows a left-turn arrow there. Its stop bar is set back at y~487, with a transverse bar spanning only this lane. A solid white line separates it from the next lane near the junction; upstream that line becomes dashed (C2) and shifts left with the centre line.

Right-turn lane: right-turn arrows at y~520 and y~735 on the satellite, and C1 shows a right-pointing arrow. A clear white stop bar crosses it at y~413. Upstream of about S6 the line on its left is dashed and the strip widens. C3, farther out, shows parking in this position, so this strip likely starts as parking or an entry area and becomes the turn lane.

Narrow buffer between two parallel white lines. C1 and C2 show flex posts standing between the two lines, separating the motor lanes from the bicycle facility. The stop bar's right end turns down along it.

Inner half of a two-lane bicycle facility on the right side. It has a bicycle symbol near y~510 and a mark further downstream (y~610). No stop bar crosses it at the junction end, while the adjacent outer half has one. That suggests the down-bound (contraflow) half of a two-way cycle track. In C1 a faint line splits the bike area between the posts and the kerb. Direction is inferred, not confirmed by a clear arrow.

Kerb-side bicycle lane with a straight-ahead (up) arrow at x~579, y~510-540, and its own stop bar at y~410 (x~563-607). C1 and C2 show a bike lane behind flex posts along the inbound kerb, next to a sidewalk with a bike-share dock.

trace.notes: The stop bars are staggered. The right-turn lane, buffer and bike lane stop at y~410-413; the left-turn lane next to the centre line has a set-back bar at y~487 (a bright transverse band confined to that lane, in building shadow), so y_centre=487 and y_curb=412. The crosswalk spans y~320-380. A large building shadow covers most of the arm, and the lightened panel was needed. Below y~780 the sunlit area is crossed by tree and crane-like lattice shadows, so the lines at S6-S7 are partly interpolated, using C2 to support the positions. The centre line bends left upstream of y~760 (408 to ~357 at S7), and the left lane line, with its dashed upstream part, follows it. Upstream positions of the left kerb and parking edge are uncertain: the kerb is hidden by shadow and parked cars. The two-way reading of the bicycle facility, and the direction of its inner half, are inferred. Street-view camera markers appear 2-4 m off (C1 and C2 actually sit in the outbound lane). S1 lies inside the junction; at S2, the crosswalk's far edge, only the kerbs are given.

strips.evidence: Strip between the left curb (x~385) and the first white line (x~420) carries a painted bicycle symbol with arrow (around x~400, y~400) on the satellite; continues as dashed bike-lane lines through the junction.
Two parallel solid white lines (x~420 and x~445) with diagonal hatching between them for the whole length: painted buffer separating the outbound bike lane from the outbound travel lane.

Single wide asphalt lane (~4.4 m) between the hatched buffer and the median's left curb, starting at the downstream edge of the crosswalk (y~295); no dividing lane line visible in sun or in the lightened shadow.

Raised curbed island with rounded nose at y~325 (planter boxes, soil), continuing as the planted tree median seen in C1 (on the photo's right) and C2 (on the left, with a yellow edge line beside its curb); its edges stay visible as faint lines in the lightened shadow down to S7.

Lane between the median curb (yellow edge line in C1/C2) and the solid white line at x~685; the stop bar crosses it at y~372. C1 and C2 show it as the through lane beside the median. A dark straight seam (utility trench patch, x~645) runs inside this lane and through the crosswalk; it is not a lane line.

Lane between the white lines at x~685 and x~739 holds a painted right-turn arrow just behind the stop bar (y~405); C1 and C2 show ONLY text and a right-turn arrow in this lane, between the through lane and the green bike lane. The x~685 line is solid with a dotted extension near C2.

Narrow strip (~1.5 m) right of the x~739 line; C1 (on the photo's left) and C2 (on the right) show it as a green-painted bicycle lane to the right of the right-turn-only lane, apparently separated by a curb or raised edge. Beyond it, at the stop bar, is the corner kerb; farther back, a separate hotel access lane or planter. The stop bar reaches x~764.

trace.notes: Both stop bar ends were measured on the satellite at y~372 (square bar from x~627 to x~764). The exit start comes from the downstream edge of the crosswalk over the outbound lane (y~291-297). From about S4 downstream, the building shadow covers the inbound side and the right half of the road: lines there were read from the lightened panel and are fainter, especially the x~739 line and the outer edge at S7. S1 lies inside the junction, so only the continuous left curb is given there. At S2 the median has not yet started (nose at y~325) and the inbound lane lines start only at the stop bar. The right-most boundary is the outer edge of the inbound bike lane. Beyond it, the street views show a separate hotel access/drop-off lane (a car stands on it near y~690, x~865), a planter and a tree lawn. That area is outside the Broadway carriageway and is not traced. Street-view camera positions appear about 2 m right of the lanes the photos show (C2 is in the through lane next to the median).
